slides.1.title: Three layers of texts
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The old system
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The 1957 decree, Decree 58-223 of 1958 and the AOC orders of 1958 to 1989
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The new law
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Law 99-57 of 1999 covers all farm products, and the old implementing texts stay in force until replaced
slides.1.highlights.2.title: International
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The seven Lisbon registrations of 1974 cover only the regions that existed then

Short answer: why must you still read the orders of 1958 to 1989 after Law 99-57 of 1999 took effect?
Article 37 repealed the 1957 decree but kept its implementing texts in force until replaced
Each AOC's area and rules are set in those orders

Article 37 of Law 99-57 repealed the 1957 decree but kept the texts made under it in force until new rules replace them. Each AOC's area and conditions are in the orders of 1958 to 1989, and the 2001 order still cites them.
Short answer: how do Kélibia and Mornag differ in the international register?
Kélibia is registered for Muscat wine and mistelle; Mornag for red, rosé and white
Kélibia is an AOC; Mornag was then a VDQS
Kélibia is in Nabeul; Mornag was in Tunis and South Tunis

Kélibia is registered as an AOC covering Kélibia and Tazerka in Nabeul, for Muscat wine and Muscat mistelle. Mornag was registered as a VDQS covering Mornag, Hammam-Lif and Kabouti in Tunis and South Tunis, for red, rosé and white.
